sections.title: What you know
sections.content: You know three ways to state a condition that did not happen in the past. You know *hubiera* from B1 Unit 35: *Si lo hubiera sabido, habría venido*. You know the version without *si* from B2 Unit 10: *Hubiera salido antes, habría llegado*. And you know *de haber* + participle from B2 Unit 10: *De haberlo sabido, habría venido*. All three say the same thing; they differ in tone.

sections.title: One condition, three forms
rows: Si hubiera salido antes, habría llegado.
If I had left earlier, I would have arrived. (the usual form)
Had I left earlier, I would have arrived. (no *si*, more emphatic)
De haber salido antes, habría llegado.
Had I left earlier, I would have arrived. (shorter, more written)

sections.title: What is new
sections.content: *De haber* + participle has no person ending, so it takes its subject from the main clause: *De haber salido antes, habría llegado* is about "I", because of *habría*. If the subject is different, say it: *De haber salido tú antes, habríamos llegado*. For the negative, put *no* before *haber*: *De no haber salido tan tarde, habríamos llegado a tiempo*. Pronouns attach to *haber*: *de haberlo sabido*, *de haberme avisado*.

items.spanish: De haber revisado el puente, no habría ocurrido el derrumbe.
items.english: Had they checked the bridge, the collapse would not have happened.

items.spanish: De no haber llovido, la fiesta habría sido en el patio.
items.english: Had it not rained, the party would have been in the courtyard.

items.spanish: De haberme avisado, habría ido contigo.
items.english: Had you told me, I would have gone with you.

sections.content: After *de* the verb is always the infinitive *haber*: say *De haber salido*, never *De hubiera salido*. In the other two forms *hubiera* is the verb and it needs a person: *hubiera salido*, *hubieran salido*.
